policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'there come to Jesus from Jerusalem Pharisees and scribes' is anarthrous, but ASV does not render the Greek article mechanically before a plural class noun; the presence or absence of οἱ is not distinguished by the English.
ASV renders the pair in the order 'Pharisees and scribes', matching Φαρισαῖοι καὶ γραμματεῖς rather than the reversed γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι.
ASV 'they wash not their hands' shows a possessive, but ASV regularly renders an articular body part as a possessive without italics, so the English does not decide whether αὐτῶν stood in the text.
ASV 'For God said, Honor thy father' renders a bare verb of speaking with no 'commanded, saying'; εἶπεν is distinguished from ἐνετείλατο λέγων.
ASV begins the apodosis 'he shall not honor his father' with no coordinating conjunction; the clause-initial καὶ of the longer reading is unrendered.
Future indicative τιμήσει and aorist subjunctive τιμήσῃ after οὐ μὴ both yield ASV 'he shall not honor'; the English does not distinguish them.
ASV text reads 'his father' alone, and the mapped textual note 'Some ancient authorities add or his mother' places ἢ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ in the margin, not the text.
ASV text reads 'the word of God' (τὸν λόγον), with the competing noun relegated to the margin ('Some ancient authorities read law'); ἐντολήν 'commandment' is not the rendered text.
ASV opens the citation 'This people honoreth me with their lips' with no 'draweth nigh unto me ... with their mouth' clause, so the longer RP expansion is not rendered.
ASV 'Then came the disciples' has no possessive 'his'; αὐτοῦ is unrendered.
ASV renders a past tense, 'and said unto him', rather than the historic present 'say' it uses for λέγουσιν; the aorist εἶπον is what the English shows.
ASV 'they are blind guides.' renders no dependent genitive; both readings with τυφλῶν ('guides of the blind') are excluded, leaving τυφλοί εἰσιν ὁδηγοί.
ASV 'Declare unto us the parable' carries no demonstrative; ταύτην would give 'this parable'.
ASV 'And he said' uses a pronoun subject with no name; the added Ἰησοῦς is unrendered.
ASV 'Perceive ye not' lacks the 'yet' that Οὔπω requires.
ASV 'and cried, saying' has no indirect object 'unto him'; the RP reading's αὐτῷ is unrendered.
Nominative υἱός used for address and vocative υἱέ are both rendered 'thou son of David'; English does not mark the case.
ἠρώτουν and ἠρώτων are orthographic variants of the same imperfect; 'besought him' renders either.
ASV 'worshipped him' is a simple past that renders imperfect προσεκύνει or aorist προσεκύνησεν alike.
ASV lists 'the lame, blind, dumb, maimed', matching χωλούς, τυφλούς, κωφούς, κυλλούς; every other candidate orders the four classes differently.
ASV 'at his feet' uses a pronoun; τοῦ Ἰησοῦ would give 'at Jesus' feet'.
ASV 'the multitude wondered' is singular, rendering τὸν ὄχλον rather than the plural τοὺς ὄχλους.
ASV includes 'the maimed whole' in the list of what the multitude saw; κυλλοὺς ὑγιεῖς is present in the rendered text.

ASV supplies 'and' between the members of the list idiomatically ('the maimed whole, and the lame walking, and the blind seeing'); the English does not show whether this particular καὶ stood in the Greek.
ASV 'And the disciples say unto him' has no possessive 'his'; αὐτοῦ is unrendered.
ASV 'And he commanded the multitude to sit down' is finite, but ASV routinely resolves a circumstantial participle into a coordinated finite verb, so παραγγείλας and ἐκέλευσεν are both compatible.
ASV 'commanded the multitude' is singular, matching τῷ ὄχλῳ against the plural τοῖς ὄχλοις.

ASV strings 'and he took ... and he gave thanks and brake' as finite verbs throughout, a pattern it produces from participles as readily as from finite forms; ἔλαβεν and καὶ λαβών are not distinguished.
The 'and' in ASV's chain of clauses is part of its coordinating rendering of the verse's participles and cannot be tied to this καὶ in particular.
ASV 'and gave to the disciples' renders imperfect ἐδίδου and aorist ἔδωκεν identically.
ASV 'gave to the disciples' has no possessive 'his'; αὐτοῦ is unrendered.
ASV 'and the disciples to the multitudes' is plural, matching τοῖς ὄχλοις against the singular τῷ ὄχλῳ.
The readings differ only in whether ἦραν precedes or follows its object; ASV 'and they took up that which remained over of the broken pieces' fixes English word order regardless.
ASV 'the borders of Magadan' transliterates Μαγαδάν, not Μαγδαλά ('Magdala').
